[Faithfulness]: You are given the full conversation, the question of the current turn, the assistant's answer, and documents. You should evaluate how faithful is the assistant's answer to the information in the document and previous conversation.
[Appropriateness]: You should evaluate if the assistant's answer is relevant to the question of the current turn and if it addresses all the issues raised by the question without adding extra information.
[Completeness]: You should evaluate whether the assistant's answer is complete with information from the documents.

Begin your evaluation by comparing the assistant's answer against the reference answer in this turn. Be as objective as possible, and provide a detailed justification for your rating. After providing your explanation, you must rate the response on a scale of 1 to 10, strictly following this format: "Rating: [[rating]]", for example: "Rating: [[5]]".

[The Start of Previous Conversation]
user: I got a check from my cousin from another country. Can I cash it in the USA?
assistant: I do not have much information  on cash a check from another country here in the USA but you can cash a check from another country in the USA. However, the process and fees may vary depending on the bank. Some banks may charge a collection fee and the currency exchange rate may not be the best. Another option would be to cash the check at check cashing places, but that would most likely require you being in the US. 
user: Could I cash a check from the USA overseas?
assistant: It is unlikely to cash a check from the USA overseas unless it is deposited into a US bank account in your name. You can cash US checks in almost any decent bank anywhere in the world, but it may cost you some and will probably take 2-3 weeks. Additionally, if the check is earned in the US, you would need to file a tax return with the IRS and send them a payment.
user: OK. Thank you!
assistant: You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. Let me know if you have any other questions.

user: what about international transfers, is it easy to do ? How much do the banks charge do to them?
assistant: International wire transfers can be done through banks, but the process and fees may vary. Banks typically charge a fixed fee for sending and receiving international wires, and may also include a margin on the exchange rate. The exact fees can depend on the bank and the country involved. For example, in Turkey, the charges are generally low with a fixed charge of around 15 Euros for both sending/receiving banks. Alternatively, there are peer-to-peer services like Transferwise that offer lower fees for international money transfers. These services often split the transfer into two domestic transfers, with the international part and currency conversion happening internally, which can make the process faster and more cost-effective.
user: Can a foreigner open a bank account in the USA?
assistant: Yes, a foreigner can open a bank account in the USA, but the requirements may vary depending on the bank. Some banks may require a US address, identification such as a US Driver's License, and proof of foreign address and identification. It is also worth noting that some banks may be more willing to open an account for a foreigner than others. It may be necessary to contact several banks and inquire about their specific requirements.

user: And about Americans, can they open an account in another countries?
assistant: Yes, Americans can open a bank account in another country, but the requirements may vary depending on the country and the bank. Some countries may require a local address, identification such as a passport, and proof of residence. It is also worth noting that some countries may have restrictions on non-residents opening bank accounts. For example, some banks in Germany allow non-residents to open an account with a passport and an address in the country, while others may require additional documentation. For an American it nearly impossible to open a Swiss bank account. It is very important to know that the US is one of the only countries which taxes its citizens on global income.Compliance is so big an issue that foreign banks are turning away US customers rather than having to comply with FATCA, leaving people unable to open a bank account. 
user: Thank you. I even do not have money even to open an account here. 
assistant: I understand that you might be facing financial difficulties. Do you have any other question?
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Yes. Can you tell me about Bank of America. I am considering to open an account there
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
 Bank of America is part of the clearXchange bank network, which allows customers to send money to anyone for free with just their email address or phone number if both parties use one of the participating banks. This includes Wells Fargo, so you can easily transfer money from a Wells Fargo account to a Bank of America account using Wells Fargo's SurePay, and vice versa.

[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
The document provides limited information about Bank of America: it says the bank participates in the clearXchange network, allowing free transfers using an email address or phone number when both people use participating banks. It cautions that the participating-bank list may change. [S1]

However, the evidence does not cover account types, opening requirements, minimum deposits, or monthly fees, so I cannot determine whether an account would suit your budget or whether you qualify to open one.
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]

"Wells Fargo and Bank of America both belong to the clearXchange bank network (https://www.clearxchange.com/about).  You can send money to anyone for free with just their email address or phone number if you both use one of these banks: (Check the list on the clearXchange website, as the above list may change.) That means you can easily transfer money from a Wells Fargo account to a Bank of America account using Wells Fargo's ""SurePay"".  To go the other direction, on the Bank of America website click on the ""Transfers"" tab, then go to Send Money To Someone -> ""Using their email address or mobile number""."

 Here are some.  Did you know about the Montreal Exchange (MX)?  The MX is part of the TMX Group, which owns both the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) and the Montreal Exchange. You'll find lots of Canadian equity and index options trading at the MX.  If you have an options trading account with a decent Canadian broker, you should have access to trade options at the MX. Finally, even considering the existence of the MX, you'll still find that a lot of Canadian companies don't have any options listed.  Simply: smaller and/or less liquid stocks don't have enough demand for options, so the options exchange & market makers don't offer any.

To answer your last question, yes I would strongly suspect that finance would be more lucrative than school counselling. But is that 46k starting?I'm non-US but that sounds pretty good to me. Also, you don't need an MBA to start getting experience in finance. If your degree is from a different discipline you just need some extra way of signalling that you're interested and capable.
